On Android, Firebase requires C/C++ and Java components
that are distributed with the Firebase and Android SDKs.

It's likely the required dependencies for Firebase were not included
in your Unity project.
Assets/Plugins/Android/ in your Unity project should contain
AAR files in the form firebase-*.aar
You may have disabled the Android Resolver which would
have added the AAR dependencies for you.

Do the following to enable the Android Resolver in Unity:
* Select the menu option 'Assets -> Play Services Resolver -> 
  Android Resolver -> Settings'
* In the Android Resolver settings check
  'Enable Background Resolution'
* Select the menu option 'Assets -> Play Services Resolver ->
  Android Resolver -> Resolve Client Jars' to force Android
  dependency resolution.
* Rebuild your APK and deploy.

On iOS, Firebase requires native (C/C++) and Cocoapod components
that are distributed with the Firebase SDK and via Cocoapods.

It's likely that you did not include the require Cocoapod
dependencies for Firebase in your Unity project.
You may have disabled the iOS Resolver which would have added
the Cocoapod dependencies for you.

Do the following to enable the iOS Resolver in Unity:
* Select the menu option 'Assets -> Play Services Resolver ->
  iOS Resolver -> Settings'
* In the iOS Resolver settings check 'Podfile Generation' and
  'Add Cocoapods to Generated Xcode Project'.
* Build your iOS project and check the Unity console for any
  errors associated with Cocoapod tool execution.
  You will need to correctly install Cocoapods tools to generate
  a working build.

ACTk offers own collection of the secure types to let you protect your variables from ANY memory hacking tools (Cheat Engine, ArtMoney, GameCIH, Game Guardian, etc.).
Below you can try to cheat few variables of the regular types and their obscured (secure) analogues (you may change initial values from Tester object inspector):

ACTk has secure layer for the PlayerPrefs: <color="#75C4EB">ObscuredPrefs</color>. It protects data from view, detects any cheating attempts, optionally locks data to the current device and supports additional data types.
Below you can try to cheat both regular PlayerPrefs and secure ObscuredPrefs:
PlayerPrefs: easy to cheat, only 3 supported types
ObscuredPrefs: secure, lot of additional types and extra options
ACTk is able to detect some types of cheating to let you take action on the cheating players. This example scene has all possible detectors and all of them are automatically start on scene start.
Allows to detect Cheat Engine's speed hack (and maybe some other speed hack tools) usage.
Time Cheating Detector (updates once per 1 min by default)
Allows to detect system time change to cheat some long-term processes (building progress, etc.).
Detects cheating of any Obscured type (except ObscuredPrefs, it has own detection features) used in project.

Detects common types of wall hack cheating: walking through the walls (Rigidbody and CharacterController modules), shooting through the walls (Raycast module), looking through the walls (Wireframe module).
Allows to detect foreign managed assemblies in your application.
